summary: First test pass for Part 2 of the Action Assignment Fix (attendee dropdown + AI assignee->user_id mapping + strict carry-over matching). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter91_assignment.py (12 tests: unit coverage of _match_attendee_user_id, unit coverage of _get_rolled_actions strict user_id matching incl. the Part 1 manager-exclusion regression, and live API tests that PUT /api/review/{id}/actions and /learning_needs pass assigned_to_user_id through and persist it, verified via GET). All 12 pass. Also converted /app/backend/tests/test_carryover_fix.py into a real pytest test (it previously ERRORed under the configured `-n 2 --dist loadscope` because the module ran asyncio.run at import time on both workers, so each worker saw the other worker's seeded meeting) — now 13/13 pass. Browser-driven UI testing on the real report page (manager, meeting c20802af 'Supervision with Demo User') confirmed: 'Assigned to' is a <select> in BOTH Add Action and Add Learning Need, populated with the meeting's actual attendees (Demo Manager / Demo User) with user_id as the option value; selecting an attendee saves and renders 'Assigned: Demo User · Due: 2026-10-01'; persists across reload; leaving the dropdown unselected saves with no assignee; LN complete-toggle and remove buttons still work. All test data cleaned up (DB verified clean). MAIN FINDING: the AI-extraction mapping is almost certainly dead code in practice — analyze_meeting() is never given the attendee list, so the model returns whatever name it hears in the transcript (usually a first name or a role word), while _match_attendee_user_id requires exact whole-string equality with the attendee's full name. Probed all existing analyses in the DB: 0 of 14 real AI-extracted assignee names would map to a user_id.

minor.issue: AI assignee->user_id mapping will rarely fire. (a) analyze_meeting() receives only the transcript — attendee names are never passed into the prompt (contrast diarize/map_speaker_numbers_to_names, which DO get them), so extracted assigned_to values are transcript-derived first names/roles ('Connor', 'Priya', 'Manager', 'Tracy'). (b) _match_attendee_user_id only does exact case-insensitive full-string equality, so 'Sarah' will never match attendee 'Sarah Thompson'. Empirically: 0/14 existing AI-extracted assignee names in the DB would map (probe: backend/tests/_iter91_probe_aimatch.py). Fix suggestion: pass the attendee name list into the analysis prompt and ask for canonical names, and/or add unique first-name/token matching in _match_attendee_user_id.

Behaviour change worth confirming as intended: an action now linked (via the new dropdown) to a MANAGER/ADMIN-role attendee can never carry over, because the strict branch requires assigned_to_user_id to be in new_supervisee_ids (managers/admins are filtered out). Under the old fuzzy-name path such an action would have rolled over when the manager's name was among the new attendees. Verified by test_only_actions_for_present_supervisee_roll_over (a_linked_mgr excluded). If managers are expected to be assignable via the dropdown (they are listed in it), their outstanding actions will silently never surface again.

Both accept raw dicts with zero validation — any client can store arbitrary keys/types, and assigned_to_user_id is never validated against the meeting's attendee list (a manager could POST an arbitrary UUID or an assigned_to name that contradicts assigned_to_user_id). Consider a light Pydantic model / server-side attendee check now that carry-over depends on this field being trustworthy.

design_issues.screen: Evidence/Overview tab — Add Action / Add Learning Need forms
issues: The assignee control is a raw native <select> (browser default styling, native chevron) while the rest of the app uses shadcn-styled inputs; it looks visually inconsistent next to the adjacent styled text inputs.

Minor: the dropdown lists ALL attendees including manager/admin roles, but actions assigned to a manager can never carry over (see backend note) — consider either excluding them or making the consequence clear.

action_items: Make the AI mapping actually work: pass meeting attendee names into analyze_meeting()'s prompt and/or extend _match_attendee_user_id with unique first-name/token matching (currently 0/14 real extracted names map).
Decide/document whether manager-assigned actions should ever carry over; today linking an action to a manager attendee permanently excludes it from carry-over.
Optionally validate assigned_to_user_id server-side against the meeting's attendees in PUT /review/{id}/actions and /learning_needs.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/processing.py: _match_attendee_user_id is the weakest link of Part 2 — exact full-name equality against names the model was never shown. Add a fallback (single-token match that resolves to exactly one attendee) and log unmatched assignee names so the gap is observable.

routers/processing.py: the loop sets item['assigned_to_user_id'] unconditionally (overwriting to None when unmatched). Fine today, but if analyze_meeting ever starts returning the field itself, this silently discards it — use setdefault-plus-match semantics.

routers/processing.py: learning_needs items get no generated 'id' (actions do). The frontend falls back to the array index as the React key, so reordering/removal can mis-key rows. Cheap to fix in the same loop.

Test-infra note: /app/backend/pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope, so any test module doing work at import time runs twice concurrently. test_carryover_fix.py did exactly that and errored; converted to a test function + run-scoped assertion.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the in-scope Part 2 flows (action + learning need dropdowns, save, persistence, unassigned case, toggle/remove regression)

seed_data_creation: Unit tests seed a synthetic previous meeting + analysis (ids prefixed test-i91-*, synthetic user ids) and delete them in fixture teardown. UI/API tests added TEST_ / TEST_UI actions and learning needs to existing meetings c20802af... and f00bf65f... and removed them; DB re-verified clean (no test-% meetings/analyses, no TEST_UI rows remaining).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Part 2 creation-time assignment (dropdown) is fully verified end-to-end and needs no re-test unless changed. The one unverified scenario is a LIVE AI pipeline run producing assigned_to_user_id — not run because it costs a 30-90s transcription+analysis and, on the available seeded audio, the transcript names (Connor/Priya) can never match the attendee names (Demo Manager/Demo User); the mapping helper itself is unit-tested. Reusable suite: backend/tests/test_iter91_assignment.py (module-scope manager session fixture with MFA bypass; auto-picks an in_review meeting with an analysis and restores its original actions/learning_needs on teardown). Good target meeting for UI work: c20802af-17e3-4210-b497-13d09c9e67ec (in_review, attendees Demo Manager + Demo User). Remember pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope.
rca_of_the_issue: Part 2 implementation is correct for everything in scope: EvidenceTab renders <select> elements (data-testid new-action-assigned / new-ln-assigned) built from meeting.attendees with user_id as the option value, MeetingReport.addAction and EvidenceTab.addLN send assigned_to_user_id, and the raw-dict PUT endpoints persist it verbatim (confirmed via GET). _get_rolled_actions strict-matches assigned_to_user_id against the new meeting's supervisee ids and still falls back to fuzzy name matching for legacy actions, and the Part 1 manager-exclusion regression still holds. The only real gap is the AI-extraction half of the feature: the analysis prompt is never given the attendee roster, so extracted assignee strings are transcript first-names, which cannot satisfy the exact full-name equality in _match_attendee_user_id — measured 0/14 matches across every analysis currently in the database. The test_carryover_fix.py 'failure' the request mentioned was a test-harness artifact of pytest-xdist running the module's import-time asyncio.run on two workers simultaneously; running it directly always passed, and it now passes under pytest after conversion.
